public.S0: On 17 March 2022 the Security Council adopted resolution 2626 (2022) by 14 votes in favour, none against and one abstention by the Russian Federation.
public.S1: In paragraph 4 the Council decides to extend the UNAMA mandate until 17 March 2023. In paragraph 7 it requests the Secretary-General to report to the Council every three months on Afghanistan and implementation of the UNAMA mandate, including at the subnational level.

S2.speaker: Norway
S2.passage: Norway, the penholder, said the new mandate would have UNAMA promote inclusive political dialogue, monitor and report on human rights and help facilitate humanitarian and basic needs assistance. It said UNAMA should engage all Afghan actors on these issues, including the Taliban.
fields: supports inclusive dialogue and human rights work
includes the Taliban among the Afghan actors engaged

S3.speaker: Russian Federation
S3.passage: Russia explained its abstention by stressing that the agreement of the host country to the UN presence was important and that a reference to it met opposition during drafting. It additionally argued for more substantive cooperation with the Taliban authorities and said the lack of a reference could impair UNAMA's effectiveness.
fields: links the host-country agreement concern to its abstention
records that reference to agreement faced opposition or was omitted
records Russia's call for more substantive cooperation with the Taliban authorities as Russia's position

S4.speaker: China
S4.passage: China welcomed the renewal and urged the country concerned to expedite the unconditional return of Afghan assets to the Afghan people. It also expressed doubts about whether the resolution's priorities were appropriate and its tasks balanced and called for timely review and potential adjustment.
fields: called for expedited unconditional return of Afghan assets to the Afghan people
expressed doubts about priorities or balance and wanted timely review or adjustment
